transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you too, and, um, thank you so much for fitting me in. I know you're probably very busy. 

Well, I'm here because... I guess I've been having a little trouble at work lately. Nothing major! I'm a health services manager and my team is great, things are mostly fine, but... 

Well, to be honest, the main reason I’m here is that anything that takes real, focused, sitting-down brain work... like the monthly reports, or if I have to sit and plan out a big multi-site health event... it just feels like I hit a wall. I end up putting it off, even when I know how much it matters. 

I feel a bit embarrassed even saying that out loud, to be honest. I mean, at my age, I should just be able to sit down and do my job, right? I just don't want to let my staff down. Does that make sense? I'm just hoping maybe you might have some advice on how I can handle it better.
Has this difficulty with staying focused on tasks been something you've struggled with for most of your life, or is this a more recent development?

Well... um, I suppose if I'm being completely honest, it's not entirely new. I really don't want to make it sound worse than it is, because I've always managed to get by okay, you know? But, um, even way back in elementary school, I guess I had some trouble with this sort of thing. 

My teachers would always tell my parents that I was a bright kid—which was nice of them to say!—but they also said I was just... always daydreaming. I used to lose my worksheets all the time, or I'd just completely forget to turn in my homework. Not on purpose, or to be rebellious or anything! It just somehow wouldn't make it out of my bag unless my mom checked my backpack every single night to make sure things actually got handed in. 

I feel a little foolish bringing up things from when I was a little kid, honestly. Is... is that the kind of information you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.
Beyond these difficulties with focus and organization, do you find yourself frequently feeling restless, on edge, or unable to stop worrying about multiple different things in your daily life?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say so. I don't really feel jittery or on edge like that. I'm actually a pretty relaxed guy, for the most part! 

I mean, I care about my work and my team, of course, so I want to do a good job, but I don't really sit around worrying about a million different things, if that makes sense. It's really just the... the sitting down and focusing part that trips me up. I'm usually pretty calm otherwise, not really restless at all. 

I hope that's helpful? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information to figure this out.
Do you often find yourself feeling the need to move around, like fidgeting with your hands or feet, or do you find that you have trouble staying seated when it is expected?

Oh, um, no, not really. I mean, I don't think I'm a fidgety person at all. I can sit through long meetings just fine, honestly! I might tap my pen every now and then, but who doesn't do that, right? 

I definitely don't have trouble staying in my seat or anything like that. I'm usually the one quietly sitting there, just... well, maybe zoning out a little bit if it's a really dry presentation, but I'm definitely not jumping up and pacing around the room. I try to be very respectful of other people's time in meetings. 

Does that answer what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm not missing the point of your question.
In your daily life outside of work, do you often find yourself losing important items like your keys, phone, or wallet, or perhaps forgetting about planned appointments or social commitments?

Well, um... I guess I do have a few moments where things sort of slip my mind, but I really try my best to keep on top of it all. I don't want to sound like I'm completely disorganized or anything! It's just... well, outside of work, I help out with some community stuff, and lately I've, um... I've been forgetting to return calls from some of our volunteers. And sometimes I'll miss picking up little things for events while I'm out running errands. 

It's not that I don't care about it, I really do! It's just that it gets a bit overwhelming sometimes, and things fall through the cracks. There was... well, once or twice, I actually had to apologize to the group because a community meeting completely slipped my mind until someone texted me asking where I was. I felt so terrible about it, I really did. I hate letting people down like that. 

I try to write things down now so it doesn't happen again. I hope that doesn't make me sound too irresponsible? I really am trying to be better about it. Is that the sort of thing you meant?
